spec: DESIGN.md — installations, the machine seam, standalone save cards (issue #181)
description: Whole fixture machines in; the canonical SavefilePlacement serialization (atlas/contract.py) out, asserted with exact equality — for catalogue entries whose launch command names a standalone emulator a packaged save card covers. The card is the thin cited half (atlas/data/standalone_saves.json); the resolver reads the emulator's own configuration the way the emulator does, at the revision the arrangement ships (Dolphin 2603a). Root kind is emulator_directory: no frontend hands these emulators a save root.

vectors.name: dolphin-keeps-one-gci-folder-per-region-and-the-region-is-a-hole
vectors.rationale: The GCI-folder device sits in slot A (Dolphin.ini [Core] SlotA = 8, the registered default), so a GameCube save is one .gci file in <GC user>/<region>/Card A — named from the save's own directory entry, which no read of the content path recovers. The answer's dir keeps the <region> segment as a hole a caller with metadata fills, while the groups list all three region trees so a caller without it still sees the whole candidate set. RetroDECK reroutes the region trees with symlinks; the emulator-view dirs are the answer's.

vectors.name: xemus-saves-live-inside-the-emulated-hard-disk
vectors.rationale: Every Xbox save lives on the emulated hard disk — a disk image xemu.toml names, which the arrangement keeps beside the firmware. The image is one shared file; per-title structure exists only inside its FATX filesystem, so the save-inside-image caveat states the layout machine-readably (UDATA/<title id>) for a tool that can parse it, and a file-level client backs the image up whole. The EEPROM rides as its own named settings group.

vectors.name: emudeck-the-cemu-launcher-leads-to-the-appimages-config
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's catalogue launches Cemu through its own launcher script, so the script's basename is the identity the command states — the same save card the %EMULATOR_CEMU% token reaches. The launcher picks its binary at run time, AppImage first (cemu.sh:85-93 probes ~/Applications, vars.sh:4-5), and the AppImage reads the host's own XDG tree (emuDeckCemu.sh:13) — so the answer resolves settings.xml there, and the per-title unit templates below the configured MLC.

vectors.name: retrodeck-azahars-emulated-sd-holds-one-save-directory-per-title
vectors.rationale: The arrangement wires Azahar by configuration, not symlinks: qt-config.ini's [Data Storage] group (spelled Data%20Storage in the file) sets use_custom_storage and routes sdmc_directory into the saves tree, read the way the emulator reads it — the \default companions included (ReadSetting, config.cpp:1442-1450). Below the SD the unit is one directory per title: Nintendo 3DS/<ID0>/<ID1>/title/<save_id>/data/00000001, ID0/ID1 compile-time zeros (archive.h:22-24), the id the game's own (archive_source_sd_savedata.cpp:21-29) — granularity per-game-directory, and extdata stated beside it as its own group, keyed by an id no title id fills.

vectors.name: retrodeck-duckstations-slot-pair-keys-the-card-by-title
vectors.rationale: DuckStation's answer is the Dolphin GC shape spoken in its own vocabulary: two slots, each picked by CardXType, the pair as granularity.mode. The arrangement ships PerGameTitle/None with the memory-card directory wired into the saves tree — so slot 1 is one <save_id>_1.mcd per game (the sanitized database title, with the playlist/disc-set preference stated, system.cpp:3688-3742) and slot 2 holds nothing. A game DuckStation cannot title falls back to the shared card, and the caveat says so.

vectors.name: retrodeck-pcsx2s-two-file-cards-share-their-images
vectors.rationale: PCSX2's slots are read the way the emulator reads them: [Folders] MemoryCards names the card directory (wired into the saves tree here), [MemoryCards] SlotN_Enable and SlotN_Filename pick each card, and the type is what sits at the card's full path (FileMcd_SetType, MemoryCardFile.cpp:584-604 at v2.6.3) — nothing there means a file card that would be created on first use, one shared .ps2 image per slot. Both console ports answer as shared-card groups; the six multitap slots stay silent while disabled.
